nodes.name: Cu foam pretreatment
nodes.procedure: Cu foam was immersed into 1M HCl and acetone, respectively, to remove the oxide layer and organic residues on the surface of Cu foam, and then washed with deionized water and ethanol several times before being finally dried in a vacuum oven at 60°C for 12h.
nodes.source_text: Cu foam was immersed into 1M HCl and acetone... dried in a vacuum oven at 60°C for 12h.

nodes.name: In situ Cu(OH)2 nanowire growth
nodes.procedure: Cu foam was immersed into the freshly prepared mixture of NaOH (2.67M) and (NH4)2S2O8 (0.13M) for 25 min without stirring.
nodes.source_text: Cu foam was immersed into the freshly prepared mixture of NaOH (2.67M) and (NH4)2S2O8 (0.13M) for 25 min without stirring.

nodes.name: Cu2O nanowire formation
nodes.procedure: The as-prepared CF@Cu(OH)2 NW was further annealed under Ar at 450°C with a heating rate of 2°C/min for 2h to obtain CF@Cu2O NW.
nodes.source_text: The as-prepared CF@Cu(OH)2 NW was further annealed under Ar at 450°C with a heating rate of 2°C/min for 2h to obtain CF@Cu2O NW.

nodes.name: CoFe LDH electrodeposition (1 min)
nodes.procedure: CoFe LDH was grown on the surface of CF@Cu2O NW by electrodeposition at a constant potential of -1V with deposition time of 1 min in a three-electrode system (Pt foil counter, SCE reference, CF@Cu2O NW working) using electrolyte prepared by dissolving 3.492g Co(NO3)2·6H2O and 3.336g FeSO4·7H2O in 80 mL water, N2 saturated.
nodes.source_text: CoFe LDH was grown on the surface of CF@Cu2O NW by electrodeposition at a constant potential of -1V with different deposition times (1, 3, and 5 min).

nodes.name: CoFe LDH electrodeposition (3 min)
nodes.procedure: CoFe LDH was grown on the surface of CF@Cu2O NW by electrodeposition at a constant potential of -1V with deposition time of 3 min. The electrodeposition was performed in a typical three-electrode system consisting of Pt foil, saturated calomel electrode (SCE), and the prepared CF@Cu2O NW as the counter electrode, reference electrode, and working electrode, respectively. The electrolyte was prepared by dissolving 3.492g of Co(NO3)2·6H2O and 3.336g of FeSO4·7H2O in 80 mL of water. The electrolyte was saturated by N2 during the electrodeposition process.
nodes.source_text: CoFe LDH was grown on the surface of CF@Cu2O NW by electrodeposition at a constant potential of -1V with different deposition times (1, 3, and 5 min).

nodes.name: CoFe LDH electrodeposition (5 min)

nodes.procedure: CoFe LDH was grown on the surface of CF with the same method of CF@Cu2O NW/LDH-3.

nodes.description: OER performance in 1.0 M KOH under dark
nodes.source_text: the resultant CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3 photoelectrode exhibits the best OER performance, with the lowest overpotential of 347 and 396 mV at the current densities of 100 mA cm⁻² and 200 mA cm⁻², as well as the smallest Tafel slope of 130.4 mV dec⁻¹

nodes.description: OER performance in 1.0 M KOH under illumination
nodes.source_text: Under illumination, the overpotentials of the resultant CF@Cu₂O NW, CF@LDH-3, and CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3 photoelectrodes decrease by 31, 8, and 14 mV at the current density of 100 mA cm⁻²

nodes.description: HER performance in 1.0 M KOH under dark
nodes.source_text: the resultant CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3 photoelectrode exhibits the best HER performance, with the lowest overpotential of 104 and 263 mV at the current densities of 10 mA cm⁻² and 100 mA cm⁻², as well as the smallest Tafel slope of 99.68 mV dec⁻¹

nodes.description: HER performance in 1.0 M KOH under illumination
nodes.source_text: Under illumination, the overpotentials of the resultant CF@Cu₂O NW, CF@LDH-3, and CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3 photoelectrodes decrease by 52, 19, and 15 mV at the current density of 10 mA cm⁻², corresponding to light enhancements of 23.8, 9.2, and 14.4%

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in 1.0 M KOH two-electrode cell
nodes.source_text: the alkaline electrolytic cell based on the optimal CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3 requires an operating potential of only 1.62 V to drive a high current density of 100 mA cm⁻² under illumination. Meanwhile, a current density retention of up to 91.62% can be reserved after a stability test for 24 h

The corresponding C_dl values of the resultant CF@Cu₂O NW, CF@LDH-3, CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-1, CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3, and CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-5 photoelectrodes can be determined to be 11.17, 5.56, 32.69, 59.21, and 39.63 mF cm⁻²

nodes.source_text: LSV was also performed to evaluate the HER property for Pt/C, where an overpotential of 32 mV was required to reach only a current density of 10 mA cm⁻²

nodes.characterization_summary: FESEM shows necklace-like Cu₂O NW with rough surface and slightly decreased diameter after pyrolysis, and nanosheet-structured CoFe LDH on CF@Cu₂O NW surface for CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: nanowires with a smooth surface are clearly observed (Figures 2a,d, and S1c), which can be converted into a necklace-like structured Cu₂O NW with a rough surface and slightly decreased diameter after pyrolysis (Figures 2b,e, and S1d) ... Further electrodeposition achieves the growth of nanosheet-structured CoFe LDH on the surface of CF@Cu₂O NW (CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3: Figures 2c,f, and S1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM demonstrates core-shell structured Cu₂O/CoFe LDH with Cu₂O NW core diameter of 150 nm and CoFe LDH nanosheet shell thickness of 300 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM result clearly demonstrates the core-shell structured Cu₂O/CoFe LDH (CF@Cu2O NW/LDH-3: Figure 2g), where the core Cu₂O NWs exhibit an average diameter of 150 nm and the CoFe LDH nanosheet shells demonstrate an average thickness of 300 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes at heterostructure interface with interplanar spacing of 0.213 nm (Cu₂O (200)) and 0.261 nm (CoFe LDH (012)).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) results demonstrate that the lattice fringes in the heterostructure interface with the interplanar spacing of 0.213 and 0.261 nm belong to the (200) crystal plane of Cu₂O and the (012) crystal plane of CoFe LDH (Figure 2h)

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms presence of Cu, Fe, Co, and O in CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH photoelectrode with Cu mainly on inner nanowires and Co/Fe on outer nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) result indicates the presence of Cu, Fe, Co, and O in the resultant CF@Cu2O NW/LDH photoelectrode (Figure 2i), which can be clearly demonstrated by the EDS element mapping (Figure 2j).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows diffraction peaks at 29.5°, 36.4°, 42.3°, 61.4°, and 73.5° assigned to Cu₂O (JCPDS no. 99-0041) and additional peak at 29.5° attributed to CoFe LDH (JCPDS no. 50-0235).
nodes.evidence_snippet: there are several diffraction peaks in 29.5, 36.4, 42.3, 61.4, and 73.5° assigned to Cu₂O (JCPDS no. 99-0041) after pyrolysis under Ar. An additional peak at 29.5° appears, which can be attributed to CoFe LDH (JCPDS no. 50-0235).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Cu⁺ at 932.7/952.3 eV and Cu²⁺ at 934.8/954.8 eV for CF@Cu₂O NW with negative shift after CoFe LDH deposition; Co²⁺ at 781.0/796.6 eV and Fe³⁺ at 711.6/724.6 eV for CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3 with positive shifts indicating electron transfer from Co/Fe to Cu.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HR XPS spectra of Cu 2p for the resulting CF@Cu₂O NW photoelectrode can be fitted into three pairs of peaks belonging to two different states (+1 and +2) of Cu ... there is a positive shift of ca. 0.1 eV in the binding energy of Co 2p and Fe 2p for the resultant CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3 photoelectrode.

nodes.characterization_summary: UV-vis DRS shows strong absorption in UV-vis range for all photoelectrodes with band gaps between 1.9-2.0 eV from Tauc plots.
nodes.evidence_snippet: all of the resultant photoelectrodes exhibit strong adsorption in the UV–vis range. Furthermore, ... all the resultant photoelectrodes possess a similar band gap between 1.9 and 2.0 eV (Figure 4b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Mott-Schottky shows negative slope for p-type Cu₂O (flat band 1.398 eV) and positive slope for n-type CoFe LDH (flat band 0.345 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: There is a negative slope for the resultant CF@Cu₂O NW, whereas there is a positive slope for CF@LDH-3 ... the flat band potential of Cu₂O and CoFe LDH can also be measured to be 1.398 and 0.345 eV, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: PL spectra show emission peak at 540 nm; CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3 exhibits weakest emission indicating lowest recombination efficiency.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The PL spectra results show strong emission peaks at 540 nm ... The resultant CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3 exhibits the weakest emission intensity among all the CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH photoelectrodes

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faradaic region determines double-layer capacitance C_dl = 59.21 mF cm⁻² for CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3, indicating largest ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding C_dl values of the resultant CF@Cu₂O NW, CF@LDH-3, CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-1, CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3, and CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-5 photoelectrodes can be determined to be 11.17, 5.56, 32.69, 59.21, and 39.63 mF cm⁻², respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3 has smallest charge transfer resistance; illumination reduces resistance further.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Among all the samples, the resultant CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3 photoelectrode possesses the smallest radius in the high frequency region ... the resultant CF@Cu₂O NW/LDH-3 photoelectrode also exhibits a decrease in charge transfer resistance to a certain extent under illumination

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR performed at X-band frequency of 9.84 GHz on resultant photoelectrodes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron paramagnetic spectroscopy (EPR) was performed from an EPR spectrometer (A300, Bruker) at an X-band frequency of 9.84 GHz, sweep width of 100.00 G, and center field of 3510.00 G.
